title: Smooth locus and boundary divisor from completed curve singularities
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $Z$ be an integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $S=S_{\mathrm{reg}}\amalg S_{\mathrm{node}}$ be a finite set of closed points [def-weil-closed-points] of $Z$, partitioned into disjoint subsets. Assume $Z\setminus S$ is smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. At every $s\in S_{\mathrm{reg}}$ assume $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Z,s}\cong k[[t]]$, and at every $s\in S_{\mathrm{node}}$ assume $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Z,s}\cong k[[u,v]]/(uv)$, as complete local $k$-algebras; completions and power series are [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].
Let $
u:N	o Z$ be the normalization in its function field [def-sc-normalization]. Then $
u$ is finite, $N$ is integral and is a proper smooth connected curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves], the nonsmooth locus of $Z$ is exactly $S_{\mathrm{node}}$, and $
u$ is an isomorphism over $Z\setminus S_{\mathrm{node}}$, including over $S_{\mathrm{reg}}$. The reduced inverse image of $S$ is the effective Cartier divisor $B=\sum_{p\in
u^{-1}(S)}[p]$ on $N$: its support is finite, each coefficient is one, and its ideal at a point $p$ of its support is the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{N,p}$. Its associated invertible module is $\mathcal O_N(B)$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle], with its canonical trivialization off $
u^{-1}(S)$. No ambient curve or adjunction line is part of the hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), final completion-regularity/smoothness argument; varieties.tex Tag 0C45 (lemma-normalize-noetherian-dim-1) for normalization geometry, supplemented by lem-sc-normalization-properties and lem-sc-point-cartier. Agent synthesis for a marked integral curve.

proof.text: The scheme $Z$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied to $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. In particular every $A_s=\mathcal O_{Z,s}$ is a Noetherian local ring. By the field case $d=1$ of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], $k[[t]]$ is regular local. The regularity equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local], transported through the assumed complete-local-ring isomorphism, therefore makes $A_s$ regular for every $s\in S_{\mathrm{reg}}$.

source.place: Tag 07NY, lemma-completion-regular; algebra.tex Tag 032C, remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian

proof.text: For $s\in S_{\mathrm{node}}$, put $R=k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. Its elements $\bar u$ and $\bar v$ are nonzero and $\bar u\bar v=0$: setting $v=0$ gives a homomorphism $R\to k[[u]]$ sending $\bar u$ to $u\ne0$, and setting $u=0$ proves the other assertion. These evaluations are ring homomorphisms directly from the coefficient multiplication in [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Thus $R$ is not a domain, hence not regular local by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local] and the stipulated isomorphism $\widehat{A_s}\cong R$, $A_s$ is not regular. This does not assert that $A_s$ itself has zero divisors: the integral curve may have an analytically reducible node.

source.place: Tag 00NP, lemma-regular-domain, and more-algebra.tex Tag 07NY, lemma-completion-regular; explicit quotient evaluations written by the worker

proof.text: Set $U=Z\setminus S_{\mathrm{node}}$, an open subscheme since the removed set is a finite set of closed points. At every point of $U\setminus S_{\mathrm{reg}}=Z\setminus S$ the local ring is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], applied to the assumed smooth open subscheme $Z\setminus S$. At the remaining points use step 1. Hence $U$ is regular by the locally Noetherian stalk criterion in [def-weil-regular-scheme]. An algebraically closed field is perfect (every algebraic extension is trivial), so [lem-trf-regular-perfect-field-smooth] applies to $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, which is locally of finite type, and makes $U$ smooth. Conversely a smooth neighbourhood of a point in $S_{\mathrm{node}}$ would have regular local ring there by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], contradicting step 2. The nonsmooth locus is exactly $S_{\mathrm{node}}$.

source.place: Tags 056S, lemma-smooth-regular, and 0B8X, lemma-dense-smooth-open-variety-over-perfect-field; properties.tex Tag 02IT, lemma-characterize-regular

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-normalization-properties] to the integral finite-type $k$-scheme $Z$. It gives that $\nu$ is finite, surjective and birational, that $N$ is proper with $\dim N=\dim Z=1$, and that $N$ is smooth because $k$ is perfect. The normalization construction [def-sc-normalization] makes $N$ integral: on each nonempty affine of $Z$ its normalization ring is an integral-closure subring of the common function field $k(Z)$, hence a domain, and these affine pieces have the same generic point. Therefore $N$ is nonempty and irreducible, and thus connected: two disjoint nonempty open subsets contradict irreducibility. Properness includes separatedness and finite type. These properties make $N$ a proper smooth connected curve in [def-sc-curves].

source.place: Tags 0BXR, lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic; 0C45, lemma-normalize-noetherian-dim-1; 0B8Y, lemma-regular-point-on-curve; assembly through lem-sc-normalization-properties

proof.text: The regular open subscheme $U$ of step 3 is normal by clause (1) of [rem-pc-regular-normal]. Clause (b) of [lem-sc-normalization-properties], with this very open $U\subset Z$, now gives $N\times_ZU\xrightarrow{\sim}U$. Thus $\nu$ is an isomorphism over $Z\setminus S_{\mathrm{node}}$, in particular at all the marked regular points. No isomorphism at a node, and no assumption that all marked points are singular, has been used.

proof.text:
Let $T=
u^{-1}(S)$ as a set. Every fibre of $
u$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], so $T$ is a finite union of finite sets and is finite. It is closed as the inverse image of the finite closed set $S$. Each point of $T$ is closed in $N$: by the birationality in step 4 the generic point of $N$ maps to the generic point of $Z$, not to $S$; let $p\in T$ with $
u(p)=s$. By continuity $
u(\overline{\{p\}})\subseteq\overline{\{s\}}=\{s\}$, so $\overline{\{p\}}$ lies in the finite fibre over $s$. In this finite set choose $q\in\overline{\{p\}}$ with $\overline{\{q\}}$ minimal; any $q'\in\overline{\{q\}}$ has $\overline{\{q'\}}=\overline{\{q\}}$, hence $q'=q$ as a scheme is $T_0$, so $q$ is closed. If $p$ were not closed, then $q
e p$ and, $p$ not being the generic point, $\{q\}\subsetneq\overline{\{p\}}\subsetneq N$ would be a chain of irreducible closed subsets of length two, contradicting $\dim N=1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Thus $T$ is a finite set of distinct closed points.

source.place: Tags 02NU, lemma-finite-quasi-finite, and 02NH, lemma-quasi-finite; elementary dimension-one specialization argument

proof.text: Form the effective divisor $B=\sum_{p\in T}[p]$ of [def-sc-divisor], with each point occurring once. Since $N$ is a smooth connected curve and every $p\in T$ is closed, [lem-sc-point-cartier] makes every reduced point $[p]$, and hence this finite sum, effective Cartier. Near a fixed $p\in T$ remove all the other finitely many closed points of $T$. On this neighbourhood $B$ is just the reduced point $p$, so its stalk ideal is exactly $\mathfrak m_p\subset\mathcal O_{N,p}$; outside $T$ its ideal is the unit ideal. In particular $B$ is reduced and has support $T$. The reduced inverse image of $S$ has the same ideals: on such an affine neighbourhood its radical ideal is the prime ideal of the sole closed point $p$, since a radical ideal is the intersection of the primes in its vanishing set. Consequently this reduced inverse image is $B$, and all coefficients are one. The assertion concerns the reduction, not possible multiplicities of the unreduced fibre.

source.place: Tag 0B8Y, lemma-regular-point-on-curve; divisors.tex Tag 0AG8, lemma-effective-Cartier-in-points; explicit finite disjoint-support assembly

proof.text: Write $\mathcal I_B$ for this Cartier ideal. By [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] its associated module is $\mathcal O_N(B)=\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_N}(\mathcal I_B,\mathcal O_N)$. Where $\mathcal I_B=(f)$ with $f$ a non-zero-divisor, the map sending a homomorphism $h$ to $h(f)$ identifies this dual with $\mathcal O_N$: for any $a$ its inverse is $fr\mapsto ar$, well-defined because multiplication by $f$ is injective. Hence the module is locally free of rank one, i.e. invertible [def-sc-invertible-module]. On $N\setminus T$ the ideal is canonically $\mathcal O_N$; evaluation at $1$ gives the canonical trivialization of its dual there. This includes $T=\varnothing$, when $B=0$ and the trivialization is global.
